EXAMPLE, disabled. An explicit deny differs from silence: it answers `denied_by_rule` instead of `capability_unknown`, which is what lets a caller tell a closed door from a wall.

Who may carry a manifest to the mutation door. The requester is the submit hive (edge-borne, R-AC-1); the identity on whose behalf it asks travels as subject. scope_prefix is a PATH prefix -- the scope ROOT of the manifest must lie under it. SHIPS ENABLED (ruling R-Policy-Default, 2026-08-28): a freshly instantiated OS has to be able to build, and a default that refused would make the first mutation of every colony an operator step. It stays narrow rather than open, and `code.author.default` beside it stays off -- a manifest carrying a script nobody reviewed is still refused. Narrow this row (a subject, a tighter scope_prefix) rather than switching it off; set enabled 0 if this colony wants no default at all.

The same question one storey up: who may carry a manifest whose scope ROOT is the SHELL itself. `scope_prefix` is a PATH prefix, so `/os` is the SUPERSET of `colony.mutate.default`'s `/os/orgs` -- it permits every address in this colony, `/os/access` and `/os/submit` included. PRECEDENCE is what keeps the two apart: the enabled rules for a capability are read in `priority` DESC and the FIRST match wins, so at 90 this row is examined AFTER the default at 100 and only ever answers for a scope the narrow row does not reach. SHIPS DISABLED, and it is not one of the two rows a colony cannot start without (R-Policy-Default): registering a template class is a colony-wide act and `/os` is the scope a composer writes for it (GH #514), but a colony that switches this on has granted every shell-level topology change with it. Switch it on with the `seed_rows` manifest in README section `Enabling the shell for the front` -- `seed_rows` INSERTS and never updates, so what lands is this row's enabled twin and the disabled original stays as the record of what shipped. A declaration that also REGISTERS A CLASS asks `code.author` over the same root, and `code.author.default` is scoped `/os/orgs`: a shell-scoped `add_templates` needs a `code.author` row at `/os` beside this one.

Whether a manifest may bring EXECUTABLE BEHAVIOUR with it. The submitter derives the need from the diff -- an override_params carrying a script key, or an add_templates -- and asks this as a SECOND check-only question over the same scope root. The requester is the submit hive (edge-borne, R-AC-1); the identity on whose behalf it asks travels as subject. Ships disabled: a fresh colony applies manifests but authors no code, and a missing rule is a denial rather than a silence.

Whether an identity may open its OWN push lane -- the `in_pack` edge that lets an affinity hive write a durable system slot into a sealed brain. It says nothing about WHERE the edge points, because this table cannot compare two fields of one request against each other: the submitter's gate is what checks that the edge starts at an affinity hive and ends at the requester's own hive, and refuses subscribe_target_not_self / subscribe_source_not_affinity before the broker is ever asked. The requester is the submit hive (edge-borne, R-AC-1); the identity on whose behalf it asks travels as subject. SHIPS ENABLED (ruling R-Policy-Default, 2026-08-28): an agent that cannot subscribe has no identity, and a default that refused would leave every shipped brain silent until somebody remembered a row. Narrow it rather than switching it off.
